Climbing Out of Iron and Silver

Low-elo games are won by the team that makes fewer mistakes, not by flashy plays. Learn what actually wins games in Iron and Silver, the habits that hold most players back, and a simple routine to practice.

How low-elo games are really decided

In Iron, Bronze and Silver, most games aren't won by one amazing play. They're lost by the team that makes more mistakes: more deaths, more missed minions, more fights started for no reason.

That's good news. You don't need perfect mechanics to climb. You need to make fewer mistakes than the average player at your rank, game after game. A player who farms steadily, rarely dies and takes free objectives will win more often than a player with great reflexes who throws once per game.

Remember too that you're the only player who is in every one of your games. Your four teammates change each time, and over many games the bad teammates are spread evenly between both teams. The one thing that's always on your side is you.

The four things that win games

  1. Farming. Minions are the most reliable gold in the game. Most low-elo players miss half their CS, so simply last-hitting well puts you an item ahead without a single kill. Start with Last-Hitting 101.
  2. Not dying. Every death gives the enemy gold, costs you farm and experience, and leaves your team a player short. A 2/1 player often helps the team more than a 6/8 player. See Staying Alive: Map Awareness for Beginners.
  3. Taking towers and dragons. Kills don't win games; destroying the Nexus does. After you win a fight or kill your lane opponent, hit the tower or start the dragon instead of wandering off. Turret plates stay on the tower all game now, so a tower is always worth gold, and the first turret of the game gives a bonus to everyone nearby. Read Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron for the timers.
  4. Playing few champions. If you know one champion's combos, matchups and build by heart, your hands are free to watch the map. If you play a new champion every game, all your attention goes to your own buttons.
Pro tipAfter every kill, ask "what can we take now?" The answer is usually a tower, a dragon or the enemy jungle camps. A kill that doesn't turn into something is only half used.

Habits that hold most players back

These five habits lose more low-elo games than anything else. You probably have at least one of them. Everyone does.

  • Chasing. You follow a low-health enemy into the fog and run into their jungler, or you chase them past their tower. Three people chasing one enemy across the map while the rest of the enemy team takes Baron is a classic low-elo loss.
  • Fighting without vision. Walking into a dark jungle or river to start a fight means you don't know how many enemies are waiting. If you can't see them, assume they're there. See Vision Basics: Wards and the Minimap.
  • Ignoring the wave. Leaving lane to help in a fight that's already over, while a big wave crashes into your tower, costs gold and sometimes the tower itself. Learn the basics in Wave Management: Push, Freeze and Crash.
  • Tilt. After one bad death, you take a risky fight to "make up for it," die again, and the game snowballs from there.
  • Blaming. Typing at a teammate never makes them play better, and while you type, you're not watching the map.
Common mistakeChasing a kill because the enemy is "only at 50 health." That last bit of health has started more lost fights than any other number. If you can't kill them in a few seconds and they're running toward their side of the map, let them go and take their wave or tower instead.

Tilt and blame: protect your own game

You can't control what your teammates do. You can control whether their mistakes become your mistakes too.

  • Mute early. If chat bothers you, mute it at the start of the game. You keep pings and lose nothing important.
  • Use the death timer to look, not to type. Watch where the enemies are and plan where you'll go when you respawn.
  • Games at this rank are long and messy. Teams throw leads all the time. A game that looks lost at 15 minutes often turns around at 30 because someone gets caught. Keep farming and wait for the enemy's mistake.
  • Set a stop rule. For example, stop after two losses in a row. Tilted games are where most LP disappears.

The The Mental Game: Tilt, Focus & Improving guide goes deeper into tilt, goals and reviewing your games.

A simple practice routine

You don't need hours of practice. A small routine, repeated every session, beats random games.

  1. Warm up for five minutes. Use our Last-Hit Trainer or a Practice Tool game to get your timing back before you queue.
  2. Pick one CS goal. For example, 50 CS at 10 minutes. Once you hit it most games, raise it to 60, then 70. Check your number with Tab at 10:00.
  3. Review your deaths. After the game, think through each death (or watch it in the replay) and ask one question: "What could I have seen or done earlier?" Write down one lesson and focus on it next game.
  4. Keep a small champion pool. One main role, two or three champions. Our champion guides mark difficulty, so start with the easier ones.

If you're not sure what to learn next, follow the learning path: it lists every guide and practice tool in order.

Measure progress the right way

Your rank goes up and down from day to day, and one session tells you very little. Instead, track things you control:

  • Your CS at 10 minutes.
  • How many times you died before 15 minutes.
  • Whether you met your one goal for the game.

If those numbers improve over a few weeks, your rank follows. Players who climb out of low elo usually aren't the most talented ones. They're the ones who fixed one habit at a time and kept going.

Key takeaways

  • Low-elo games are lost by the team with more mistakes, so make fewer of them.
  • Farm well, die less, and turn every won fight into a tower or dragon.
  • Stop chasing, don't fight in unwarded areas, and don't leave a big wave crashing into your tower.
  • Mute chat if it tilts you, and stop after two losses in a row.
  • Warm up, set one CS goal, review your deaths, and play two or three champions.
